serial_dictatorship.name: Picking rounds
serial_dictatorship.tagline: Everyone picks in turn, in a drawn order.
serial_dictatorship.how: A turn order is drawn — from the poll token, so anyone can verify it. Each person, in turn, receives their favourite among what's left.
pros: Impossible to game: ranking sincerely is always best
Very easy to explain and accept
cons: The last in line inherit the leftovers
Luck weighs heavily on the outcome

optimal_sum.name: Maximum satisfaction
optimal_sum.tagline: The allocation that pleases the most people, computed exactly.
optimal_sum.how: Each allocation "costs" the rank it holds in the person's list (1st choice = 0, 2nd = 1…). The Hungarian algorithm finds the allocation with the minimal total cost: the best overall satisfaction, exactly.
cons: Can sacrifice one person for the common good

top_trading_cycles.name: Trading circle
top_trading_cycles.tagline: Everyone already owns something; win-win swap cycles.
top_trading_cycles.how: Everyone already owns one thing (the Nth person on the list owns the Nth thing) and ranks all the things. The algorithm runs swap cycles on the remaining favourites until done. Nobody ends up worse than what they started with.
pros: Nobody ends up worse than at the start
cons: Exactly as many things as people
The outcome depends heavily on endowments

stable_roommates.name: Stable pairs
stable_roommates.tagline: Pairs nobody has an interest in leaving.
stable_roommates.how: Everyone ranks the other participants. Irving's algorithm looks for stable pairs: no two people would mutually prefer each other over their assigned partners. It can prove that no stable pairing exists — the fallback is then announced: picking rounds in a drawn order.
pros: No pair wants to "run off" together
cons: A stable pairing doesn't always exist
Ranking everyone can take a while

gale_shapley.name: Two groups (Parcoursup)
gale_shapley.tagline: Two sides rank each other; a stable matching.
gale_shapley.how: Two groups rank each other (candidates and programmes, mentees and mentors…). Deferred acceptance (Gale-Shapley) produces a stable matching: no duo would mutually prefer each other over their assignment. Side 1 proposes — the method favours it; each side-2 entry can host several people (capacities).
pros: Handles capacities (several spots per side-2 entry)
Ranking sincerely is optimal for side 1
cons: Side 2 may be tempted to rank tactically
Some stay unmatched if spots run out

fptp.name: First-past-the-post
fptp.how: Everyone votes for a single candidate. Whoever gets the most votes wins, even without an outright majority.
pros: Just one trip to the ballot box
cons: A winner rejected by 60% of voters

runoff.name: Two-round runoff
runoff.how: If no one reaches 50%, the top two face off in a second round. The final winner is bound to have an absolute majority.
pros: You can vote with your heart in round one
cons: The third-placed could be a better consensus

condorcet.name: Simple Condorcet
condorcet.how: Everyone ranks the options. We simulate every head-to-head duel: the winner is the one who beats all the others.
cons: A longer ballot to fill in

condorcet_random.name: Randomised Condorcet
condorcet_random.tagline: Condorcet, with chance breaking the deadlocks.
condorcet_random.how: Like Condorcet, but when the duels go round in circles (A>B>C>A), the winner is drawn at random from the deadlocked loop.

mj.name: Majority judgment
mj.tagline: You grade, the majority grade wins.
mj.how: Everyone gives each option a grade (from "Reject" to "Excellent"). The option with the highest median grade wins.
pros: Expresses nuance, not just a choice

approval.name: Approval voting
approval.how: Everyone ticks as many options as they approve of. The one approved by the most people wins.

borda.name: Borda count
borda.how: Everyone ranks the options. First place earns n-1 points, second n-2, and so on. Add them up: most points wins.
pros: Takes the whole ranking into account

proportional.name: Proportional representation
proportional.how: Instead of a single winner, seats are shared out in proportion to the votes (d'Hondt method). Ideal for an assembly.

indirect.name: Electoral college
indirect.how: Voters are split into constituencies. Each picks a local champion — by whichever count you choose — who sweeps up its electors. The highest elector tally wins.

list.name: Party-list vote
list.tagline: The leading list takes half the seats, the rest go proportionally.
list.how: You vote for a whole list (as in French local elections). The list that comes first automatically receives half the seats — the majority bonus — then the other half is shared proportionally among every list above 5%, bonus included.
pros: Delivers a stable majority to govern

AiDoc.title: Placet for AI assistants
AiDoc.intro: Placet turns a group decision into a structured vote. You can generate a link that opens a pre-filled draft: the user reviews it, tweaks it, then launches. No authentication is required to produce the link.
AiDoc.slackTeaserBody: Start a vote without leaving your channels: /placet builds the vote, people vote on the web, and the result comes back to the channel.
AiDoc.paramDescription: — optional context (place, budget, deadline…), shown under the question and in the share preview.
AiDoc.paramOptions: — 2 to 8 options separated by |. Prefix each option with an emoji: it becomes the icon (e.g. 🍕 Italian|🍣 Japanese).
AiDoc.paramMedia: — optional: one http(s) illustration URL per option (image, video, doc), in the same order as options, separated by | (leave an option blank for no illustration). Only real, reliable URLs — don't make them up; when in doubt, leave it empty. For many images, prefer the API.
AiDoc.paramPlaces: — optional: one MAP link per option (Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, Apple Maps), in the same order as options, separated by |. Options located this way show up on a map under the vote. Different from media (illustration): a place is situated, an illustration is looked at.
AiDoc.paramNotes: — optional: one short comment per option (why it is on the list), in the same order as options, separated by | — one line, no pipe inside.
AiDoc.paramDates: — time-slot vote: replaces options with a list of ISO dates/times separated by | (e.g. 2026-07-12T20:00|2026-07-13T12:30). Recommended method: approval (single winner only).
AiDoc.paramMethod: — a key from the table below (default: simple_vote).
AiDoc.paramSurvey: — SURVEY: survey=1 turns the result into an opinion panorama with no declared winner (ideal to measure opinions or map a situation). Prefer approval (prevalence) or majority_judgment (intensity).
AiDoc.paramScale: — SCALE (majority judgment): scale= picks the grades assigned to each option — agreement, severity (what weighs), frequency, satisfaction, dissatisfaction, priority. Default: electoral grades ("Reject … Excellent").
AiDoc.paramAssign: — ASSIGNMENT instead of a vote (allocate things, form pairs): replaces method with one of serial_dictatorship (picking rounds), optimal_sum (maximum satisfaction), top_trading_cycles (trading circle), stable_roommates (stable pairs, even count), gale_shapley (two groups, capacities). options becomes the list of things to allocate (one-sided methods only).
AiDoc.paramParticipants: — assignment participants, separated by | — each gets a personal ranking link. For gale_shapley, also add sideb: side-2 entries ("Name ; capacity"), separated by |. For duty rosters/shifts, combine assign with dates (ISO slots) and per (2 to 6): each person gets N slots, the picking order snakes back and forth.
AiDoc.paramWhy: — rationale (especially for the method choice): shown to the user to build trust.
AiDoc.formatWarning: ⚠️ Don't include any sensitive data in the URL (emails, guest lists, credentials, tokens).

SlackPage.intro: Add Placet to your Slack workspace. A /placet command builds the vote with your team; voting happens on the web (with real methods: approval, majority judgment, Condorcet…) and the result comes back to the channel.
SlackPage.step1Body: Type “/placet Where should we have lunch?” (or “/placet dates …” for time slots) in any channel.
SlackPage.step2Body: Everyone adds options and picks the method, right in the message.
SlackPage.step3Body: On launch, the channel gets the link: everyone votes on the web, no account needed.
SlackPage.step4Body: At close (button or deadline), the tally and the winner are posted to the channel.
SlackPage.permissionsNote: Placet requests the minimal permissions (commands, chat:write) to post and update voting messages. Ballots stay on the web; no voter needs an account. Type /placet help in Slack anytime.

create.prepHint: Allow twenty minutes before you start: sheets over a couple of pieces of furniture, the big lights off, and above all old devices set down in the rooms — they become the portraits of the manor.
create.screens: One screen per player, plus 3 to 5 devices set down
create.screensHint: Portraits can be very old phones, a tablet, a laptop: they show a picture and a code, nothing more. You need three at the very least, and they must stay plugged in.
create.name: Your first name

how.title: How the night goes
how.s1: You set three to five devices down in the rooms: these are the portraits. Each one shows a code that keeps changing.
how.s2: Through the evening you stand your watches: type a portrait's code into your phone, and stay in front of it for a minute and a half. That writes down where you were, and when.
how.s3: The Ghost, meanwhile, is given a moment to haunt a room. The bell tolls a little later, the house gathers, you look at who was where — and you vote. Nobody is ever eliminated.

rules.title: The rule, in one sentence
rules.body: Keeping a watch in front of a portrait proves where you were. One of you is the Ghost: when the bell tolls, the house knows where the Ghost struck, and looks for the one the register cannot place anywhere else.

Echecs.metaTitle: Collaborative chess — two teams, one move, one vote each
Echecs.metaDescription: A game of chess where each side is a group: you talk it over, you vote, and the majority move is played. No account, no player limit, works on a phone.
Echecs.name: Collaborative chess
Echecs.tagline: Two teams. One move. One vote each.
Echecs.pitch: Each side is a group. Every turn, everyone picks their move, and the one with the most votes is played. Afterwards you find out what the group decided — never who voted for what.

create.title: Open a game
create.hint: No account, nothing to install. You share the code, and everyone picks a side as they arrive.

how.title: How it works
how.one: Everyone joins the side they want, White or Black. No limit: six players or six hundred.
how.two: When it's your side's turn, everyone picks their move on the board. Nobody sees anyone else's.
how.three: Someone on the team says “we're ready”: the move with the most votes is played. You never wait for everyone.
how.four: If two or more moves tie, a second round decides between those moves only. If the tie holds, chance settles it.

sujetJour.position: One of today's characteristics is about where the country sits on the globe — not just its continent. Sweep wide before narrowing down.
sujetJour.mers: One of today's characteristics is about the sea: coastlines, oceans bordered, or no access at all. Compare a coastal country with a landlocked one; the gap talks.
sujetJour.taille: One of today's characteristics is about the country's size — its area or its population. Deliberately try a giant and a tiny one.
sujetJour.voisinage: One of today's characteristics is about the country's neighbours. A country with no border and one with ten will give you very different answers.
sujetJour.culture: One of today's characteristics is about culture: language, heritage, sport. Geography alone will not do it today.
sujetJour.etat: One of today's characteristics is about the state itself: its history, its institutions. Think regimes and dates, not just maps.
sujetJour.alliances: One of today's characteristics is about alliances: treaties, unions, organisations. Two neighbours may well not be on the same side.
sujetJour.richesse: One of today's characteristics is about the country's wealth or its currency. Two countries of the same size can part ways there.
sujetJour.ressources: One of today's characteristics is about what the country produces or holds: energy, farming, nature. Step off the political map.
sujetJour.usages: One of today's characteristics is about a way of life in the country — how people move around or live there.
sujetJour.autre: Today's characteristics are not all geographic. Vary your guesses to find out which one you are missing.
